merge.title: Consumption mask: measure it on the signing channel first, then either load-and-keep or demote it; stop presenting an unloaded PWM as a CPA/DPA defence
merge.threat: Bench CPA/DPA/TVLA attacker with a shunt or EM probe on a powered, unlocked device, targeting the ~70,754 sk_seed-absorbing SHA-256 PRF calls per C10 sign that run through the non-DPA-hardened HASH peripheral. The production fence (secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:694-725) forces `consumption-mask` on and its text says that without it the WOTS/FORS secrets are exposed to bench CPA/DPA. That overstates what the mask does: on pq1 it is a 10 kHz PWM into an NC pad (PA6, secure/src/board/pq1.rs:301-316), stepped once per ~1 ms SysTick from an xorshift32 (secure/src/main.rs:4329-4337). Into a bare pad the duty cycle does not change supply current; only frequency does (CV·f is sub-microamp at 10 kHz). So the only "hiding" layer claimed for the signing channel is, as built, almost certainly a physical no-op, and nobody has measured it. The display-SPI variant of the threat (D-06) is out of scope: a 10 kHz mask cannot touch 20 MHz bus content.
merge.proposal:
SCA-07 survives for the signing channel only, as a measurement-gated item rather than a build item. D-06 is absorbed only where it overlaps.

Step 1, measurement (bench, no pq1 board change). Add three arms to the already-planned on-silicon PRF TVLA (#228): mask off, mask on unloaded, mask on loaded. Run on iota2, where a resistor can be hung on PA5/TIM2_CH1 (round-1 says it is header-accessible; confirm on the board) from the MCU VDD domain to GND, sized inside the GPIO limit (a few mA). Use the Rigol MHO934 with a 1-10 ohm shunt and the `sca-trigger` GPIO (secure/Cargo.toml:644-652). Report max|t| and traces-to-detect for each arm, both raw and after a >100 kHz high-pass filter; the filtered number is the one that matters. Record it in docs/hardware/evt-silicon-validation.md, which today has no mask row in §9 (:908-924) even though consumption_mask.rs:48-49 and pq1.rs:314-315 say it does.

Step 2, decision gate.
- If the loaded mask gives a material, filter-robust increase in traces-to-detect: raise the pq1 hardware ask (load on PA6 on the MCU VDD domain, next spin) and do the GPDMA port as the #831/#646 fix. Port details: GPDMA1 channel in circular linked-list mode, request TIM3_UP on pq1 and TIM2_UP on iota2, destination CCR1, SEC|PRIV|SRC_SEC|DEST_SEC, table in secure SRAM, refilled from the platform TRNG (`rng::fill`, never `rng_strong`) continuously during signing. A faithful Trezor port is not enough here: Trezor refills its 119-entry table only on display refresh (consumption_mask.c:34-38, vg-2864/display_driver.c:417), so over a 7 s sign with no refresh it is a fixed 11.9 ms periodic pattern that averages out. A TRNG-fed table also removes the xorshift32, which is currently an allowlisted exception to CLAUDE.md:355 "No software PRNG".
- If not (my expectation, from an unmeasured back-of-envelope: the load adds a low-frequency term that a high-pass removes, leaving two edge transients per 100 us that touch only a few percent of PRF calls): do not add a load to pq1 and do not port GPDMA. Demote the claim instead. Reword the fence in nsc/mod.rs:694-725, CLAUDE.md, README.md:233 and red-teaming.md §6.7 from countermeasure to unvalidated noise source. Whether to keep the fence at all is an owner decision. The signing-channel SCA posture then rests on the F-16 shuffle, the per-chain cap, the PIN/dual-SE gate and the #228/#229 disposition.

Step 3, independent of the measurement (firmware and docs, small).
(a) Close #831/#646 minimally: count reseed skips, retry on the next tick instead of waiting a full 1024-tick window, add host tests for the success / all-zero / error transitions. The #831 follow-up comment measured zero lost acquires on a non-signing bench, so the bias toward signing windows is structural but unobserved; measure the skip rate under a signing workload.
(b) Land the driver half of the PRNG refactor. At HEAD, hw/consumption_mask.rs still has inline `static mut PRNG_STATE`/`RESEED_TICKS` (HEAD:138,145,194-208), while consumption_mask_prng.rs:22-42 states it has no production caller, so its tests cover a reference copy. The fix exists only as an uncommitted working-tree diff (41+/75-).
(c) `selftest_pin_toggles()` runs only under `debug-log` (consumption_mask.rs:93-110), so a shipping image never checks that the PWM reaches the pad. Either run it unconditionally with a non-fatal sticky flag, or state that it is bench-only.
(d) Fix stale claims: red-teaming.md:694 ("seeded from rng_strong"; it is the platform TRNG), red-teaming.md:306 ("masking is the only SCA mitigation today"; F-16 exists), README.md:88,261,417 and nsc/mod.rs:698 / main.rs:1408 comments ("TIM2 CH1 on PA5"; pq1 is TIM3_CH1/PA6), and the dangling §9 reference.

members.note: Refuted on feasibility in round 1 (confidence 0.82), and I agree after reading the code. The named threat is content-dependent SPI leakage at 20 MHz; the mask is a 10 kHz PWM, and the Trezor precedent defends OLED row current on T2B1/T3B1 only, a different channel. Part 1 (randomize on every flush, drawn from rng_strong) is a no-op next to the existing 1 ms cadence, and rng_strong must stay out of the display path. Part 2 (GPDMA table) and part 3 (load plus TVLA) are the same as SCA-07 (b) and (a)/(c) and are carried there, re-pointed at the signing channel and gated on measurement.

No round-1 verdict existed; I verified it myself. Its repo-evidence claims hold: unloaded NC pad, SysTick-stepped xorshift, fail-open silent reseed, stale docs, Trezor's 119-sample GPDMA table on OLED models only, and its own admission that neither vendor documents a load or a measured figure. Kept: the measurement (c), the #831/#646 fix, the doc and fence honesty outcome. Changed: order reversed to measure first on iota2, with the pq1 load and the GPDMA port conditional on the result; priority P1 to P3. Dropped: tying TIM3_CH1 to the backlight driver enable, and 'refill per display refresh' as the refill trigger.

dropped_parts: D-06 part 1, randomize() at the top of every display flush / present_frame_ex: no-op on pq1 (a 48.6 ms blit already spans ~48 duty changes) and the wrong band for a 20 MHz bus signal.

D-06, drawing the per-flush sample from rng_strong: rng_strong does SE I2C round-trips; consumption_mask.rs documents that calling it here broke se_random's init precondition, and the wizard has the SE bus live.
D-06 as a display-emanation countermeasure in any form: no supply-side mask addresses SPI bus EM. Display emanation stays with #237 and a separate cluster.

SCA-07 (a) alternative, tie TIM3_CH1 to the backlight/LED driver enable: LCM_EN (PB15) enables the I2C-controlled AW99703 boost driver (pq1.rs:118-124, 247-248). A 10 kHz random duty there modulates trusted-display brightness, loads the boost converter rather than the MCU rail, and couples a security pin to the display the FSBL fingerprint depends on (#705).
SCA-07 (b), refill the table 'per display refresh': that is Trezor's OLED-specific trigger. For signing the table must be refilled during the sign, or it becomes a subtractable periodic pattern.
Populating a load on pq1 PA6 now: PA6 is pin 16 NC, so this is a PCB respin for an effect that is unmeasured and physically doubtful. Deferred behind the iota2 measurement.

GPDMA port now, unconditionally: it polishes a pin with no demonstrated electrical effect, adds flash to an image that is 76,949 B over the slot with ui-px (34,071 B headroom without), and adds a secure DMA channel whose NS isolation is not silicon-verified (#53). Deferred behind the measurement.

P1 / 'Trezor parity on the same MCU family' framing: Trezor enables the mask only on its two OLED models and publishes no load and no measurement, so there is no vendor evidence that it protects a signing channel.
tracked_issues: #831 (open): periodic reseed fails open and silently; follow-up comment measured zero lost acquires at non-signing bench load, so the signing-window bias is unobserved; count/retry fix still open
#646 (open): make reseed degradation explicit; acceptance criteria already include host tests and 'on-silicon trace evidence before claiming masking efficacy'
#228 (open): on-silicon TVLA on the sk_seed-absorption PRF window, explicitly 'with F-16 shuffle + consumption-mask + hardware noise floor combined'; the natural home for the mask arms
#236 (open): on-silicon SCA confirmation of emulation-only sweeps; same rig
#229 (open): v2 PRF restructure, the only remaining SHA-2-preserving fix if the PRF leaks; breaks invariant #6, so next-generation only
#53 (open): GPDMA blocked from secure SRAM never verified on silicon; prerequisite for any secure GPDMA mask channel
#805 (open): no global timing jitter / RDI; adjacent, not part of this cluster
#237 (open): display-emanation side channel, seed-wizard scope; where D-06's actual threat belongs

2. The fence and doc over-claim (nsc/mod.rs:694-725 against an NC pad) and the decision whether the ship-blocker fence should stay.
3. A load on the mask pin as a pq1 board ask (conditional).
4. The GPDMA TRNG-table port with during-sign refill (conditional).
5. `selftest_pin_toggles()` running only under `debug-log`, so shipping images never check that the PWM reaches the pad.
6. The uncommitted driver half of the consumption_mask_prng refactor: at HEAD the tests cover a module with no production caller.
7. Stale docs: red-teaming.md:694 and :306, README.md:88/261/417, the PA5/TIM2 comments in nsc/mod.rs:698 and main.rs:1408, and the dangling §9 reference in consumption_mask.rs:48-49 and pq1.rs:314-315.
decision_conflicts: No conflict with the SHAKE/masked-SHA2 decision: that memory note lists consumption-mask as a retained SCA layer. If the measurement demotes the mask, the retained list shrinks to F-13/F-16/F-17 + OptRand; that must be stated to the owner, and it must not be used to reopen SHAKE or masked SHA-2.

No conflict with the recorded argument against a global RDI timer (work-todo archive ~:1950-1962): the mask is an amplitude noise source, not timing jitter. The reasoning style of that decision (measure before building) supports gating this item on measurement.
CLAUDE.md:355 'No software PRNG': the mask's xorshift32 is an allowlisted exception (per #646). A TRNG-fed table would remove it; keeping xorshift keeps the exception.

CLAUDE.md already says the mask is 'satisfied-by-construction, not demonstrated'; the fence text in nsc/mod.rs still asserts exposure to CPA/DPA without it. The two disagree, and this recommendation resolves toward CLAUDE.md.
#831 cites a 'CLAUDE.md countermeasure-timing carve-out (2026-10-08), condition (d)'. `grep carve-out CLAUDE.md` returns nothing in the current file, so do not quote that condition as contract text.
Slot budget: any GPDMA port must report its flash delta; ui-px is already 76,949 B over the 466,944 B secure slot.
hardware_asks: None now for pq1. Do not spin a board for the mask before the measurement.

Bench only (iota2): a resistor from the mask pin (PA5/TIM2_CH1) to GND on the MCU VDD domain, sized inside the GPIO current limit, plus a 1-10 ohm shunt or current probe in the MCU supply and a low-noise differential amp (already listed as missing gear in red-teaming.md:99-104).

Conditional on a positive measurement, for the EVT owner at the next spin: route PA6 (pin 16, currently NC) to a small resistive load on the MCU VDD domain close to the MCU supply pins, not on VDD1_3V3 (the isolated SE rail gated by PA8), with a DNP footprint so it can be depopulated. Budget a few mA continuous; with no battery and supercap only, check this against the power budget.

Regardless of outcome, useful for all SCA work: a shunt/jumper footprint in the MCU VDD path and an accessible trigger pad (PB3/SWO is the current sca-trigger repoint) on a bench variant of pq1; the enclosed EVT unit has neither.

`sca-trigger` wired around the PRF region (first unchecked box in #228).
A non-shipping build that can turn the mask off for the control arm (the fence allows this under `e2e-test` / `dev-testkey`).

merge.precedent: Trezor ships a consumption mask: core/embed/sec/consumption_mask/stm32u5/consumption_mask.c:26-27 (119 samples, 10 kHz), :34-38 (table filled from rng_get), :82-87 and :117-118 (circular GPDMA linked list, PRIV|SEC|SRC_SEC|DEST_SEC), :94 (TIM2_UP request), initialised in kernel (projects/kernel/main.c:162) and bootloader (projects/bootloader/main.c:336). The feature is enabled only on T2B1 and T3B1 (models/T2B1/model.toml:5, T3B1/model.toml:5), the two monochrome OLED models; no colour-TFT model has it. The table is re-randomised only from the OLED driver's display_refresh (io/display/vg-2864/display_driver.c:417). So the Trezor precedent is for OLED pixel-current leakage, not a signing power channel, and Trezor publishes neither the pin's load nor any measured dilution. Ledger's response to the OLED channel (CVE-2019-14354) was randomised screen-update parameters and inverted-pixel boxes, not a PWM mask. No vendor documents a measured mask on a hash-based signer.
merge.rationale: Novelty: the mask itself is Trezor parity (it already exists in pq1); a published loaded-vs-unloaded measurement would be beyond both vendors, but it is evidence, not a feature. Cost: the unconditional part (Step 3 fixes plus the mask arms added to an already-planned capture) is S; M covers the bench analog chain; the conditional load plus GPDMA port would make it M-L with a board spin. Priority P3: the mask does not close the PRF residual either way, the fix that would (#229) is blocked by invariant #6, and the honest-claim correction is cheap. It should rise only if the measurement shows the loaded mask works.

merge.residual_after:
Once this lands, the signing power/EM channel is honestly characterised but not closed.
- An attacker with a shunt or near-field probe still sees ~70,754 sk_seed-absorbing compressions per sign at a fixed intra-call offset through a HASH peripheral with no DPA resistance. A loaded mask at best raises the trace count for low-bandwidth global-rail measurements; it does nothing against a localised EM probe, and a high-pass filter is expected to remove most of it.
- Single-trace horizontal and template attacks are unaffected by any additive mask.
- The mask output is itself observable on the pin, so its contribution can be recorded and subtracted by an attacker who probes it.
- The only structural fix (#229, one secret compression per sign) changes every derived key and is blocked by invariant #6 for this generation. Masked SHA-2 and SHAKE are decided-closed.
- Practical exposure therefore rests on physical possession of an unlocked device (PIN + dual-SE gate), the F-16 shuffle, and the per-key signature caps, with the #228 measurement deciding whether that is enough.
- Display-bus emanation (D-06's original threat) and pre-PIN leakage of the SE tunnel keys in software AES/HMAC are untouched by this cluster.
repo_evidence: secure/src/hw/consumption_mask.rs:12-20 (CPU-stepped, 'A full DMA port is a follow-up'), :41-51 (no load on either board, dilution unmeasured), :93-110 (selftest debug-log only), :166-192 (randomize, fail-open reseed)
secure/src/consumption_mask_prng.rs:22-42 (STATUS: no production caller at HEAD), :46 (RESEED_PERIOD_TICKS 1024), :84-93 (reseed window reset before the offer)
docs/hardware/evt-silicon-validation.md:175 (mask 'must sit near/across the die supply to matter'), :757-764, :908-924 (§9 has no mask row; SCA rig not on bench)

skeptic.reason:
The core recommendation survives: measure before building, stop presenting an unloaded PWM as a CPA/DPA defence, and land the small firmware/doc fixes. All five live_defects are confirmed against the code under PROD_SHIP_FEATURES (Makefile:2718 includes consumption-mask and mode-production, so debug-log is off), with line drift and one severity downgrade. Trezor citations check out (119 samples, TIM2_UP, SEC|PRIV attrs, T2B1/T3B1 only, refresh only from vg-2864/display_driver.c:417).

It is not refuted, but it has six real holes.

1. Bypass: the mask is weaker than the merge states, even loaded. CCR1 changes once per 1 ms SysTick against a 100 us PWM period, so each duty repeats about 10 times. One SHA-256 compression is about 3 us, so a PRF call sees a constant offset or one edge. In edge-aligned PWM mode 1 the rising edge sits on a fixed 10 kHz grid; only the falling edge moves. Per-trace mean subtraction or a high-pass removes it, and the pin is attacker-observable. Trezor's design has the same property. The loaded arm is therefore very likely negative; it is worth one resistor in an already-planned capture session, not a dedicated one.

2. The over-claim fix is wrongly gated on the measurement. Rewording nsc/mod.rs:694-725 sits in Step 2's negative branch, behind #228, which is priority:low and parked with no bench chain. The same over-claim is listed as a live defect today, and consumption_mask.rs:41-51 plus the compile_error text itself (nsc/mod.rs:717-722) already admit efficacy is unmeasured. Only the comment at :694-705 ("so the signature stays uncorrelated") and the first half of the message still assert protection. The rewording should be unconditional.

3. Step 3(a) "retry on the next tick" is a regression risk. SysTick is priority 0 (main.rs:885-888). The #831 follow-up measured that a successful reseed runs about 31 nested wait_random loops inside the ISR, and #802 measured what a per-tick rng::fill costs there (about 356 us per 1 ms tick, +55% render, #780 tear bound broken). Uncapped per-tick retry under a persistent TRNG error recreates #802.

4. The conditional GPDMA port is infeasible as specified. "Refilled from rng::fill continuously during signing" at 10 kHz is about 10,000 FI-hardened TRNG words per second, and it contends for DriverGuard with the sign path's own draws. It also needs ARR (period) randomisation, not only CCR1, or the rising-edge grid stays subtractable.

5. The iota2 measurement transfers asymmetrically. iota2 is a 169-pin part with a different power network and decoupling from pq1's 48-pin UFQFPN. A negative result supports demotion; a positive result cannot justify a pq1 board spin by itself.

6. A bench prerequisite conflicts with a checked-in doc. evt-silicon-validation.md:921-923 says on-silicon power SCA needs a ChipWhisperer-Husky/ChipSHOUTER that is not on the bench; red-teaming.md:99-104 says the Rigol plus shunt and diff amp suffices. The merge asserts the Rigol path without naming the conflict.

Not checked: whether iota2 PA5 is actually reachable on a header (the merge already says "confirm on the board"), and the 70,754 PRF-call figure.
